themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 63 this week versus a baseline of 13 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 385% increase (z-score: 5.16)—suggesting a new or intensifying source of disturbance in the district this week.
evidence: 63 noise complaints (street/sidewalk) filed this week vs. 13.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
385% spike with z-score of 5.16 (statistically significant anomaly)
No corresponding Reddit or news mentions suggest residents have not yet organized public discussion
reporting_angles: What construction, event, or activity triggered the sudden noise spike this week? Interview residents and 311 complainants.
Map the 63 complaints geographically—is noise concentrated in one area or dispersed across the district?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 7 last week from a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 522% spike (z-score: 4.63)—indicating a possible surge in building maintenance failures or aging infrastructure affecting residents, especially seniors.
evidence: 7 elevator complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
522% spike with z-score of 4.63 (high statistical significance)
Community board's repeated budget requests for senior center renovations suggest aging infrastructure is a chronic concern
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings have filed multiple elevator complaints—are certain landlords neglecting maintenance?
Interview seniors and disabled residents about how elevator outages affect access to their apartments and healthcare.

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 3 last week from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)—indicating sudden blight, debris accumulation, or vacancy issues emerging this past week.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% spike with z-score of 8.69 (extreme statistical anomaly, highest severity flagged)
Timing aligns with ongoing ULURP rezoning and development projects (Constellation CB5, Baobab Village), possibly creating temporary blight
reporting_angles: Which specific lots are generating complaints? Do they overlap with active ULURP development sites or tax-foreclosed properties?
Interview residents about visible debris, dumping, or contamination; cross-reference with Department of Environmental Protection data.

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees
themes_detail.summary: Tree complaints jumped to 5 last week from 0.5 weekly average—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—while tree planting requests also surged 967% to 4 complaints, suggesting residents perceive worsening environmental conditions or are newly engaged in greenery advocacy.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score 6.36)
4 new tree requests last week vs. 0.4 baseline (967% spike, z-score 5.21)
Community board's recurring budget requests for park improvements and amenities align with this environmental concern
reporting_angles: Survey which blocks have the most tree mortality—is this related to drought, disease, or lack of Parks Dept maintenance?
Interview residents about their interest in a community tree-planting initiative; explore whether Parks Dept has capacity to respond.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 4 exactly 2 weeks ago from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% increase (z-score: 5.21)—suggesting a new pattern of unsupervised activity, gatherings, or events at district parks requiring investigation.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 5.21)
Community board's recurring budget requests for park improvements and amenities suggest parks are underfunded/understaffed
Timing suggests a specific event, gathering, or seasonal activity pattern emerged 2 weeks ago
reporting_angles: Which parks received noise complaints? Are specific parks lacking Parks Dept patrols or lighting?
Interview residents and Parks enforcement about what activities are driving noise—concerts, street vendors, gatherings, or unauthorized events.
